milestones.title: Dedicated mu exec CLI surface exists and becomes the canonical headless path
milestones.goal: A human can discover and use `mu exec` and `mu exec --json` as the canonical non-interactive surface, with legacy raw JSON paths no longer required for the mission target.

verification.expect: Targeted CLI-surface tests prove `mu exec` behavior and help text.

verification.command: Review the `mu exec` CLI parsing/routing changes against SPEC.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms the dedicated exec boundary is correct or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: Run the real CLI help and canonical exec surface in a temp workspace, then assert the terminal output documents `mu exec` and that the command path is discoverable and usable.
verification.expect: The visible CLI surface clearly exposes `mu exec` and `mu exec --json`.

verification.command: Assert from the CLI parser and command routing tests that `mu exec` resolves to the new exec path and not to legacy `--print`/`--mode json` behavior.
verification.expect: Parser and routing assertions prove the new command boundary is canonical for this mission.

milestones.notes: This milestone closes only after the dedicated exec boundary is real, discoverable, and verified through targeted tests, review, and terminal surface evidence.

milestones.title: Public exec JSON schema and event adapter normalize Mu runtime events into a stable contract
milestones.goal: Mu internal runtime events are translated into a public JSONL contract with stable dotted event names and typed item payloads, without leaking raw internal event names.

verification.expect: Targeted adapter/schema tests pass and prove normalized public event names and payload shapes.

verification.command: Review the public exec schema and event adapter against SPEC.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms the public contract is stable and not leaking raw runtime events, or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: Run `mu exec --json` against a deterministic prompt/tool fixture and inspect the emitted JSONL stream from the real CLI.
verification.expect: The visible CLI surface emits stable dotted event names and machine-readable item payloads only.

verification.command: Compare captured JSONL output against a golden fixture and assert that no raw names like `turn_start` or `tool_execution_start` appear.
verification.expect: Golden diff and assertions confirm normalization to the public exec schema.

milestones.notes: This milestone closes only after the adapter and schema are proven by tests, review, CLI evidence, and golden-diff assertions.

milestones.title: Exec JSON contract covers command execution, file changes, todo lists, generic tool calls, and failure semantics exhaustively
milestones.goal: The machine contract is exhaustive for major execution activity and preserves stdout/stderr discipline, terminal state semantics, and parser-friendly JSONL behavior.

verification.command: npm test -w @kennyfrc/mu-coding-agent -- exec-json-command-items.red.test.ts exec-json-file-change.red.test.ts exec-json-todo-list.red.test.ts exec-json-failure.red.test.ts
verification.expect: Targeted tests pass for exhaustive item coverage, stdout/stderr discipline, and terminal failure behavior.

verification.command: Review exhaustive item mapping, stdout/stderr discipline, and terminal semantics against SPEC.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms coverage is exhaustive and parser-safe, or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: Spawn the real CLI in a temp workspace, run `mu exec --json` through scenarios that trigger command execution, file changes, todo updates, and failure, then inspect `stdout`, `stderr`, and exit code.
verification.expect: The visible CLI behavior shows JSONL-only stdout, diagnostic stderr, correct exit codes, and exhaustive public item coverage.

verification.command: Assert every stdout line parses as JSON, each turn has exactly one terminal event, and command/file/todo/failure scenarios all produce the expected public item shapes.
verification.expect: Assertions prove the public machine contract is exhaustive and terminal-state safe.

milestones.notes: This milestone closes only after exhaustive public contract coverage is proven via tests, review, terminal surface checks, and JSON parsing assertions.
